lesson:prompt.capital_of__note: Question prompt. {entityName} is a localised country name from the content pack.
lesson:prompt.locate__note: Map question prompt. {entityName} is a localised name from the content pack.
lesson:feedback.correct.title: Perfect!
lesson:feedback.correct.title__note: Celebration headline after a correct answer. One word, one exclamation mark maximum.
lesson:feedback.correct.body__note: Shown under the celebration headline. {entityName} is a localised name.
lesson:feedback.correct.streak__note: Replaces feedback.correct.body once the user has answered three or more in a row correctly. Only ever shown when that is actually true — claiming a roll after one right answer is flattery, and this app states the truth.
lesson:feedback.wrong.title: You picked {chosen}.
lesson:feedback.wrong.title__note: NEVER 'Wrong!' or 'Oops!'. Names what the user chose and hands straight over to the answer — no exclamation mark, no sad emoji. It used to read "That's {chosen}.", which is fine over a country name and falls apart over anything else: on a map question with a language answer it rendered "That's Korean. The answer is English.", where the first sentence reads as a statement about the country on screen and flatly contradicts the second. Whose statement it is has to be in the sentence. See docs/design/voice-and-tone.md.
lesson:feedback.wrong.body__note: Used ONLY when a hint exists (flag descriptions). Names the right answer and gives one memorable hook.
lesson:leave.confirm: Leave lesson? Your progress is saved.
lesson:summary.perfect.title: Flawless.
lesson:summary.perfect.title__note: End-of-lesson headline when every answer was right. One word. Satisfied and closing — never urging another lesson.
lesson:summary.perfect.body: Every one right. That's not luck.
lesson:summary.perfect.body__note: Shown under the perfect-lesson headline. Credits the person, not chance.
lesson:summary.strong.title: Nice work.
lesson:summary.strong.title__note: End-of-lesson headline at 80% accuracy or better. Satisfied and closing.
lesson:summary.strong.body: That's the world a little smaller.
lesson:summary.strong.body__note: The house line for a good lesson — see docs/design/voice-and-tone.md.
lesson:summary.done.title: Lesson complete.
lesson:summary.done.title__note: End-of-lesson headline below 80% accuracy, and after running out of hearts. States the fact. NEVER 'Keep practising' or anything implying the result fell short.
lesson:summary.done.body: The tricky ones are the ones that stick.
lesson:summary.done.body__note: The most important string on this screen: it is read by someone who just got several wrong, and it must be true rather than consoling. Harder recall really does produce stronger memory. No 'but', no 'don't worry'.
lesson:summary.early.title: Stopped there.
lesson:summary.early.title__note: Headline when the user chose to finish the lesson early. Matter-of-fact. Never 'You gave up' and never a celebration — this is not a completed lesson.
lesson:summary.early.body: Everything you answered counts. Come back whenever.
lesson:summary.early.body__note: Reassures that leaving early loses nothing, because it does not — every answer is submitted. Ends on the open door.
lesson:summary.none.body: No answers to count this time. The lesson will be waiting.
lesson:summary.none.body__note: Shown when the lesson ended before a single answer, so there is nothing to total up. Never framed as a wasted trip.
lesson:summary.xpUnit__note: Unit label under the big XP number. Keep the abbreviation if it is used in the target language; expand only if 'XP' is meaningless there.
lesson:summary.stat.percent__note: Accuracy as a percentage. Some languages put a space before the percent sign — Swedish does.
lesson:summary.stat.accuracy__note: Label under the accuracy figure on the lesson summary. Max 14 characters — it sits in a narrow tile.
lesson:summary.stat.accuracy.a11y__note: Spoken label for the accuracy tile, so it is a full phrase. Leads with the count because 'seven of ten' is more useful than a percentage read aloud.
lesson:summary.stat.coins__note: Label under the coins figure on the lesson summary. Max 14 characters.
lesson:summary.stat.stronger__note: Label under the count of facts that moved up a mastery level. The product's actual promise, so it names learning rather than score. Max 14 characters.
lesson:summary.stat.stronger.a11y: {count, plural, =0 {No facts moved up a level this time} one {# fact moved up a level} other {# facts moved up a level}}
lesson:summary.stat.stronger.a11y__note: Spoken label for the 'facts stronger' tile. The zero case is neutral, never disappointed — reviewing something you already know is a normal lesson.
lesson:summary.stat.time__note: Label under the time figure on the lesson summary: time spent answering, pauses not counted. Max 14 characters. Never frame it as speed — a slow lesson is not a worse one.
lesson:summary.stat.time.value__note: The time as a stopwatch reads it, like 1:05. {seconds} arrives already padded to two digits. Change the separator only if your language writes a stopwatch time differently.
lesson:summary.stat.time.a11y: Answering time: {minutes, plural, =0 {} one {# minute} other {# minutes}}{seconds, plural, =0 {} other {{minutes, plural, =0 {} other { }}}}{seconds, plural, =0 {} one {# second} other {# seconds}}
lesson:summary.stat.time.a11y__note: Spoken label for the time tile. Each part is empty at zero, so it reads 'Answering time: 48 seconds', '1 minute' or '1 minute 5 seconds'; the middle part is only the space between the two when both are there.
lesson:summary.practised__note: Heading over the row of flags for the countries in the lesson just finished. Deliberately places the user IN the world rather than reporting on a score. Max 22 characters.
lesson:hearts.out.title: That's the last heart
lesson:hearts.out.title__note: Heading when hearts run out mid-lesson. States the fact. Never 'You failed' or 'Game over' — the user has not failed, the lesson has ended early. Max 28 characters.
lesson:hearts.out.body: You keep everything you got right. The next lesson starts with a full set.
lesson:hearts.out.body__note: The single most important string in this state. Hearts reset per lesson, so this is never a lockout — but a child who has just been stopped does not know that. Must appear BEFORE any offer to spend coins. Never mention a refill timer: there is none, the next lesson simply starts fresh.
lesson:hearts.out.revive__note: Button to spend coins and finish the current lesson. {price} is a coin amount. Buys the moment, not access — the next lesson is free either way.
lesson:hearts.out.cantAfford: {short} coins short — but the next lesson is free anyway.
lesson:hearts.out.cantAfford__note: Shown instead of the continue button when the user cannot afford it. Ends on the reassurance rather than the gap, and never links to a store: coins come from lessons, never from money.
lesson:hearts.out.finish__note: Ends the lesson and goes to the summary, keeping every answer already given. Always present, and never framed as giving up. Max 16 characters.
lesson:check.label: Check
lesson:check.label__note: The primary button under a question. Verb, imperative: grades the answer the user has selected. Tapping an answer only selects it; this commits it. Keep it one short word — it is the biggest button on the screen and appears after every question. Max 12 characters.
lesson:check.needsAnswer__note: Screen-reader hint on the Check button while it is disabled because nothing is selected yet. Explains why it cannot be pressed and what to do. Neutral, never 'You must…'. Max 32 characters.
lesson:typed.placeholder__note: Placeholder in the box a typed question is answered in. Imperative, three words.
lesson:typed.label: Your answer
lesson:typed.label__note: Accessibility label of the typed-answer box. Read by a screen reader on landing; the question above it has already said what is being asked.
lesson:typed.labelCorrect__note: Accessibility label of the typed-answer box once the answer is in and was right: the label and the verdict in one phrase, because the platform's separate hint is not announced everywhere. Short.
lesson:typed.labelWrong__note: Accessibility label of the typed-answer box once the answer is in and was not right. Calm and brief — never "wrong" or "incorrect".
lesson:typed.wrong.title: You typed {typed}.
lesson:typed.wrong.title__note: Headline on the answer sheet after a typed answer that was not right. Names what the learner typed and hands straight on to the answer, like feedback.wrong.title; no exclamation mark. {typed} is whatever they typed, shown as typed.
lesson:typed.near.title: Close enough!
lesson:typed.near.title__note: Headline on the answer sheet when the typed answer was right but for a small slip — one letter. It counts as right, so this is praise, not a correction.
lesson:typed.near.body: A small typo. It is spelled {correct}.
lesson:typed.near.body__note: Under typed.near.title. States the real spelling so the learner meets it once. {correct} is the answer from the content pack.
lesson:check.needsTyping__note: Screen-reader hint on the Check button while it is disabled because nothing has been typed. Explains why it cannot be pressed; neutral, never "You must".
lesson:pairs.title: Match the pairs
lesson:pairs.title__note: Heading of a matching exercise: four things on the left, their partners on the right. Imperative, three words.
lesson:pairs.hint__note: Under the matching exercise heading. Tells a first-time learner the whole interaction: one tap on each side makes a pair, in either order.
lesson:pairs.matched__note: Accessibility label of a card in a matching exercise once its pair is made. {first} and {second} are the two cards, e.g. "Sweden and Stockholm, matched".
lesson:placement.result.new: We'll start you gently, and move up as you learn.
lesson:placement.result.new__note: One line on the summary of the level check when the learner is placed at the start. Calm and encouraging, never "beginner" as a label or a score.
lesson:placement.result.some: We'll start you in the middle, and widen as you go.
lesson:placement.result.some__note: One line on the summary of the level check when the learner is placed in the middle.
lesson:placement.result.confident: You know your way around. We'll start you at the harder end.
lesson:placement.result.confident__note: One line on the summary of the level check when the learner is placed high. States what changes, not a rank.
lesson:placement.none: Your level stays as it was.
lesson:placement.none__note: One line on the summary of the level check when it was left before enough questions were answered to say anything.
lesson:close__note: Accessibility label for the close/pause control in the lesson header. Describes the ACTION, not the icon — it pauses rather than quitting, so a mis-tap is recoverable.
lesson:paused.title: Paused
lesson:paused.title__note: Heading on the pause overlay. One word. Never 'Are you sure?' — leaving is safe and the copy must not imply otherwise. Max 12 characters.
lesson:paused.body: Take your time. Nothing is lost.
lesson:paused.body__note: Shown when the user pauses before answering anything. Max 40 characters.
lesson:paused.kept: {count, plural, one {Your # answer is saved} other {Your # answers are saved}} — leaving now keeps them.
lesson:paused.kept__note: Shown when the user has answered at least one question. Names the count rather than saying 'your progress is safe', because a number can be checked and a reassurance cannot. NEVER warn about losing progress: abandoning keeps and submits every answer.
lesson:paused.resume__note: Primary action on the pause overlay — most taps of a close button want this. Max 16 characters.
lesson:paused.finish__note: Ends the lesson, keeping every answer given. Never framed as quitting or giving up. Max 16 characters.
lesson:progress.label: Progress
lesson:progress.label__note: Label above the lesson progress bar. Max 10 chars.
lesson:progress.value__note: What a screen reader says for the lesson's progress bar: questions answered out of the lesson's questions. Both are numbers.
lesson:hearts.remaining: {count, plural, =0 {No hearts left} one {# heart left} other {# hearts left}}
lesson:hearts.remaining__note: Accessibility label for the hearts indicator. ICU plural.
lesson:reward.xp__note: Accessibility label for the XP chip. Spoken, so it is a full phrase.
lesson:reward.coins__note: Accessibility label for the coin chip.
lesson:empty.title: You're all caught up
lesson:empty.title__note: Shown when nothing is due. Celebrate it — never a dead end.
lesson:empty.body: Nothing is due right now. Explore somewhere new?
lesson:empty.body__note: Empty state body. Always offers the next step.
lesson:prompt.capital_reverse: {valueName} is the capital of which country?
lesson:prompt.capital_reverse__note: Reverse capital question. {valueName} is a city name.
lesson:prompt.flag_of: What does the flag of {entityName} look like?
lesson:prompt.flag_of__note: Reverse flag question — the answer is a description like "a red circle on a white field". {entityName} is a localised name from the content pack.
lesson:prompt.flag_described__note: Screen-reader-safe flag question. {description} is a phrase like "a red circle on a white field".
lesson:feedback.wrong.bodyPlain__note: Used when the fact carries no descriptive hint, e.g. a capital. Still states the answer plainly — never just "wrong".
lesson:prompt.currency_of: What money do people use in {entityName}?
lesson:prompt.currency_of__note: Currency question. Deliberately plain — 'What is the currency of X?' is a phrase a ten-year-old reads past. {entityName} is a localised country name.
lesson:prompt.currency_reverse__note: Reverse currency question. Only generated when the currency belongs to exactly one country — the engine refuses it for the euro.
lesson:speed.title: Speed round
lesson:speed.title__note: Name of the timed lesson mode.
lesson:speed.body: Ten questions, {seconds} seconds each. Missing one costs nothing.
lesson:speed.body__note: Explains the mode before it starts. The last sentence matters — it is what makes the mode playful rather than punishing.
lesson:speed.remaining__note: Accessibility label for the countdown. Read on demand, never announced every second.
lesson:speed.timeUp__note: Shown when a question times out. Neutral and brief — it is the clock's doing, not a failure. NEVER 'Too slow!'.
lesson:prompt.which_country_map__note: Map question — the locator map IS the prompt, with the country picked out against the land around it. "Highlighted" rather than "shown", because the map shows several countries and only one is coloured. Never shown to a screen-reader user; tpl.location-of.mc4 tests the same fact by ear.
lesson:prompt.location_of__note: The screen-reader-safe sibling of the map question, and a good question in its own right. Answers are subregions — "Northern Europe", "West Africa". {entityName} takes the sentence form, so English gets "the United States".
lesson:answer.correct__note: Accessibility label for the option that IS the answer, once feedback is showing. The tick beside it is `aria-hidden` artwork, so without this a screen-reader user hears only the option text and has no way to tell which one was right — colour and an unlabelled icon are the whole signal on screen.
lesson:answer.wrong__note: Accessibility label for the option the user chose when it was wrong. Deliberately NOT 'incorrect' or 'wrong answer' shouted at the user — it states which option is not the answer, in the same register as the visible copy 'That's Berlin. The answer is Paris.' See docs/design/voice-and-tone.md.
lesson:prompt.language_of: What language do people speak in {entityName}?
lesson:prompt.language_of__note: Language question. Deliberately "do people speak" rather than "is the official language of" — a ten-year-old reads past the second one. Only generated for countries the dataset lists ONE language for, and only where the country name does not give the answer away (Austria yes, Sweden no) — see scripts/build-country-facts.cjs. {entityName} is a localised country name from the pack.
lesson:prompt.language_reverse__note: "Which of THESE", not "which country" — Spanish is spoken in twenty countries and the honest question is which of the four on screen. {valueName} is a language name like "Portuguese".
lesson:prompt.calling_code_of__note: Country calling code question. The answer is a string like "+46". {entityName} is a localised country name from the content pack.
lesson:prompt.calling_code_reverse__note: Reverse calling-code question. {valueName} is a code like "+46". Safe as a reverse question because E.164 gives each of these countries its own code.
lesson:prompt.area_of__note: Size question. The answer is a rounded area such as "about 380,000 km²" — the claim is the order of magnitude, never the last digit. {entityName} is a localised country name from the content pack.
lesson:prompt.area_reverse__note: Reverse size question. {valueName} is a rounded area like "about 380,000 km²". "Which of THESE" because several countries can round to the same figure.
lesson:prompt.border_count_of: How many countries share a land border with {entityName}?
lesson:prompt.border_count_of__note: Neighbour-count question. The answer is a number like "9". Land borders only — an island answers 0.
lesson:prompt.borders_of: Which of these countries shares a land border with {entityName}?
lesson:prompt.borders_of__note: Neighbour question. Exactly one option borders the country; the others are chosen never to. {entityName} is a localised country name.
lesson:prompt.landlocked_which: Which of these countries has no sea coast?
lesson:prompt.landlocked_which__note: Landlocked question. No placeholder: the country is one of the four options.
lesson:prompt.coastal_which: Which of these countries has a sea coast?
lesson:prompt.coastal_which__note: The opposite of the landlocked question: one option touches the sea and the others do not.
lesson:prompt.hemisphere_of__note: Hemisphere question. "Entirely" is load-bearing: only countries wholly inside one quarter of the world are asked. Answers read like "Northern and Eastern".
lesson:prompt.tld_of__note: Country-code domain question. The answer is a string like ".se".
lesson:prompt.tld_reverse: Which country uses the internet domain {valueName}?
lesson:prompt.tld_reverse__note: Reverse domain question. {valueName} is a string like ".se".
lesson:prompt.alpha3_of: What is the ISO three-letter code for {entityName}?
lesson:prompt.alpha3_of__note: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 question. The answer is three capital letters such as "SWE".
lesson:prompt.alpha3_reverse: Which country has the ISO three-letter code {valueName}?
lesson:prompt.alpha3_reverse__note: Reverse alpha-3 question. {valueName} is three capital letters such as "SWE".
lesson:prompt.currency_code_of: What is the ISO code of the money used in {entityName}?
lesson:prompt.currency_code_of__note: ISO 4217 question. The answer is three capital letters such as "SEK".
lesson:prompt.currency_code_reverse: Which of these countries uses the currency code {valueName}?
lesson:prompt.currency_code_reverse__not: Reverse ISO 4217 question. "Which of THESE" because several countries share a code — the engine refuses it for the euro.
lesson:prompt.native_name_of: What do people in {entityName} call their own country?
lesson:prompt.native_name_of__note: Endonym question. The answer is the name in the country's own language, sometimes in its own script, such as "Sverige".
lesson:prompt.native_name_reverse: Which country do its own people call {valueName}?
lesson:prompt.native_name_reverse__note: Reverse endonym question. {valueName} is a country's name in its own language.
lesson:prompt.company_from__note: "Which country?" question about a company such as "Toyota". {valueName} is the name from the content pack, never translated. The answer is a country.
lesson:prompt.company_of: Which of these companies is from {entityName}?
lesson:prompt.company_of__note: "Which of these?" question about a company such as "Toyota". Exactly one of the four is from {entityName}; the others are chosen to be from other countries. {entityName} is a localised country name.
lesson:prompt.athlete_from: Which country is the athlete {valueName} from?
lesson:prompt.athlete_from__note: "Which country?" question about a sports star such as "Lionel Messi". {valueName} is the name from the content pack, never translated. The answer is a country.
lesson:prompt.athlete_of: Which of these athletes is from {entityName}?
lesson:prompt.athlete_of__note: "Which of these?" question about a sports star such as "Lionel Messi". Exactly one of the four is from {entityName}; the others are chosen to be from other countries. {entityName} is a localised country name.
lesson:prompt.musician_from: Which country is the musical act {valueName} from?
lesson:prompt.musician_from__note: "Which country?" question about a singer, composer or band such as "ABBA". {valueName} is the name from the content pack, never translated. The answer is a country.
lesson:prompt.musician_of: Which of these musical acts is from {entityName}?
lesson:prompt.musician_of__note: "Which of these?" question about a singer, composer or band such as "ABBA". Exactly one of the four is from {entityName}; the others are chosen to be from other countries. {entityName} is a localised country name.
lesson:prompt.actor_from: Which country is the actor or filmmaker {valueName} from?
lesson:prompt.actor_from__note: "Which country?" question about a film or television figure such as "Leonardo DiCaprio". {valueName} is the name from the content pack, never translated. The answer is a country.
lesson:prompt.actor_of: Which of these actors and filmmakers is from {entityName}?
lesson:prompt.actor_of__note: "Which of these?" question about a film or television figure such as "Leonardo DiCaprio". Exactly one of the four is from {entityName}; the others are chosen to be from other countries. {entityName} is a localised country name.
lesson:prompt.scientist_from: Which country is the scientist {valueName} from?
lesson:prompt.scientist_from__note: "Which country?" question about a scientist or inventor such as "Enrico Fermi". {valueName} is the name from the content pack, never translated. The answer is a country.
lesson:prompt.scientist_of: Which of these scientists is from {entityName}?
lesson:prompt.scientist_of__note: "Which of these?" question about a scientist or inventor such as "Enrico Fermi". Exactly one of the four is from {entityName}; the others are chosen to be from other countries. {entityName} is a localised country name.
lesson:prompt.writer_from: Which country is the writer {valueName} from?
lesson:prompt.writer_from__note: "Which country?" question about an author or poet such as "Astrid Lindgren". {valueName} is the name from the content pack, never translated. The answer is a country.
lesson:prompt.writer_of: Which of these writers is from {entityName}?
lesson:prompt.writer_of__note: "Which of these?" question about an author or poet such as "Astrid Lindgren". Exactly one of the four is from {entityName}; the others are chosen to be from other countries. {entityName} is a localised country name.
lesson:prompt.artist_from: Which country is the artist {valueName} from?
lesson:prompt.artist_from__note: "Which country?" question about a painter, sculptor or architect such as "Claude Monet". {valueName} is the name from the content pack, never translated. The answer is a country.
lesson:prompt.artist_of: Which of these artists and architects is from {entityName}?
lesson:prompt.artist_of__note: "Which of these?" question about a painter, sculptor or architect such as "Claude Monet". Exactly one of the four is from {entityName}; the others are chosen to be from other countries. {entityName} is a localised country name.
lesson:prompt.landmark_from__note: "Which country?" question about a place such as "Machu Picchu". {valueName} is the name from the content pack, never translated. The answer is a country.
lesson:prompt.landmark_of: Which of these places is in {entityName}?
lesson:prompt.landmark_of__note: "Which of these?" question about a place such as "Machu Picchu". Exactly one of the four is from {entityName}; the others are chosen to be from other countries. {entityName} is a localised country name.
lesson:prompt.club_from: Which country is the football club {valueName} from?
lesson:prompt.club_from__note: "Which country?" question about a football club such as "Real Madrid". {valueName} is the name from the content pack, never translated. The answer is a country.
lesson:prompt.club_of: Which of these football clubs is from {entityName}?
lesson:prompt.club_of__note: "Which of these?" question about a football club such as "Real Madrid". Exactly one of the four is from {entityName}; the others are chosen to be from other countries. {entityName} is a localised country name.
lesson:prompt.highest_point_from: {valueName} is the highest point of which country?
lesson:prompt.highest_point_from__note: "Which country?" question about a mountain such as "Mount Fuji". {valueName} is the name from the content pack, never translated. The answer is a country.
lesson:prompt.highest_point_of: What is the highest point in {entityName}?
lesson:prompt.highest_point_of__note: "Which of these?" question about a mountain such as "Mount Fuji". Exactly one of the four is from {entityName}; the others are chosen to be from other countries. {entityName} is a localised country name.
lesson:offlineStart.title: You're offline
lesson:offlineStart.title__note: Shown when a lesson cannot start: no connection, and no lesson saved for offline use yet. A fact, not an apology. Max 30 characters.
lesson:offlineStart.body: Lessons come from your account. Connect once and the next few will work offline too.
lesson:offlineStart.body__note: Under the title above. Explains why and what fixes it; never implies anything was lost (queued answers are safe).
lesson:report.cta__note: Quiet link under Continue on the answer sheet. Opens the report form. Max 24 characters.
lesson:report.title: Report a problem
lesson:report.question: What's wrong with this question?
lesson:report.question__note: Above the list of reasons. The learner picks one; there is no text box on purpose.
lesson:report.reason.wrong__note: Reason. A fact error, the most important one.
lesson:report.reason.outdated__note: Reason. Currencies and capitals do change.
lesson:report.send__note: Primary button, disabled until a reason is chosen.
lesson:report.cancel__note: Leaves the form and returns to the answer.
lesson:report.thanks.title: Thank you
lesson:report.thanks.body: We read these to fix our facts.
lesson:report.thanks.body__note: After a report is sent. Must not promise a reply or a timeline.
lesson:report.failed: That didn't send. Check your connection and try again.
lesson:report.failed__note: The report could not be sent. Keeps the chosen reason for a retry.
lesson:review.tag__note: Small tag above a question asked again at the end of a lesson because it was missed. Neutral, never "wrong". Max 20 characters.
lesson:new.tag__note: Small tag above a question about something the learner has never met. Tells them not knowing is expected; hearts are never lost on these. One short word.
lesson:summary.adventure.prompt: A little more of the world is yours. Keep exploring?
lesson:summary.adventure.prompt__note: Course continuation UI. Encouraging invitation; never a deadline or guaranteed reward. Continue adventure preserves the existing post-lesson reward flow.
lesson:summary.adventure.continue__note: Course continuation UI. Encouraging invitation; never a deadline or guaranteed reward. Continue adventure preserves the existing post-lesson reward flow.
lesson:journey.title: Your next discovery
lesson:journey.title__note: Post-lesson course reveal. The actual next available lesson comes from saved course progress; starting is optional and the home action is always available.
lesson:journey.body: Every lesson moves your adventure forward. Ready for the next one?
lesson:journey.body__note: Post-lesson course reveal. The actual next available lesson comes from saved course progress; starting is optional and the home action is always available.
lesson:journey.start__note: Post-lesson course reveal. The actual next available lesson comes from saved course progress; starting is optional and the home action is always available.
lesson:journey.home__note: Post-lesson course reveal. The actual next available lesson comes from saved course progress; starting is optional and the home action is always available.
lesson:journey.complete__note: Post-lesson course reveal. The actual next available lesson comes from saved course progress; starting is optional and the home action is always available.
lesson:feedback.correct.discovery__note: Post-lesson course reveal. The actual next available lesson comes from saved course progress; starting is optional and the home action is always available.
lesson:intro.open__note: Small quiz header button. Opens optional study cards before the first answer; never shown for a level check or speed round.
lesson:intro.title: Learn first
lesson:intro.title__note: Heading for optional study cards from the exact quiz. The learner chose to reveal these associations before answering.
lesson:intro.count: {count, plural, one {# question in this lesson} other {# questions in this lesson}}
lesson:intro.count__note: Pre-lesson teaching preview of new facts from the actual lesson. Count is total questions, not guaranteed XP.
lesson:intro.body: Study the associations in this quiz. Return to the first question when you are ready.
lesson:intro.body__note: Optional study view, opened by the learner. Returning preserves the same quiz and does not record an answer.
lesson:intro.begin__note: Primary button closes optional study and resumes the same first question. No answer or reward is recorded by this action.
lesson:intro.leave__note: Pre-lesson teaching preview of new facts from the actual lesson. Count is total questions, not guaranteed XP.
lesson:review.purpose: Try it once more to help it stick.
lesson:review.purpose__note: Learning loop guidance. Position and total are actual course steps; no invented rewards or mastery.
lesson:intro.position__note: Optional study deck navigation. Counts unique facts, not answers or earned progress.
lesson:intro.previous__note: Optional study deck navigation. Counts unique facts, not answers or earned progress.
lesson:intro.next__note: Optional study deck navigation. Counts unique facts, not answers or earned progress.
lesson:combo__note: Small badge under the progress bar after a correct answer, once the learner has three or more right in a row. Celebrates the run; never shown after a miss. Max 14 characters.
lesson:feedback.wrong.picture: The right one has the tick.
lesson:feedback.wrong.picture__note: The whole wrong-answer message when the answers are pictures (today flags; any picture pack later, so do not say 'flag'). The chosen and the right picture are already marked on screen, so this points at the tick instead of describing two pictures in words. Screen readers hear feedback.wrong.title and the body instead. Never 'Wrong!'. Max 32 characters.
